A living reference for the world, its peoples, history, places, characters, magic, visual canon, and the events of Gloin Hammerfeld's journey. This document distinguishes established facts from rumours, hypotheses, and unresolved mysteries. It is a record of the world, not a source of secret answers that have not yet been discovered. ## At a glance - World: Eryndor - Current Age: Fifth Age - Current Avarran era: Era of Crowns - Current year: 3,847 - Current campaign date: Autumn, Day 22, Year 3,847 - Current campaign time: Approximately 11:25 AM - Current campaign location: Royal Historical Archive, at Hadrik Ironvein's desk, Karak-Varn - Current protagonist: Gloin Hammerfeld, a common-born Khazari dwarf ## Canon and evidence conventions - Established: Confirmed within the world through reliable evidence or direct experience. - Reported: A statement made by a character or source that has not been independently verified. - Hypothesis: A plausible interpretation, not a confirmed fact. - Unknown: Intentionally unresolved. Do not fill gaps with invented certainty. Mysteries may remain unsolved. Gloin's ancestry, the nature of the presence beneath the mountain, and the fate of missing historical figures are not secretly predetermined. ## World and peoples ### The Seven Mountain Thrones The Khazari are a thriving dwarven civilisation of approximately 24 million people, with lifespans commonly around 300–450 years. Their seven great mountain thrones are powerful, culturally distinct and politically independent. They share deep traditions of mining, engineering, craftsmanship and runic work, but are not a single uniform kingdom. Karak-Varn is one of the Seven Thrones. Its current modeled population is approximately 22.8 million (the earlier 3.8-million baseline is superseded). It is ruled by King Durgan IV Stonehand, age 214, who has reigned for 86 years. Khazari engineering is highly developed: gyrocopters, runic machinery, artillery, armoured land engines, siege machinery, steam and hydraulic systems. Gyrocopters are rare and expensive. The technological feel blends mythic craftsmanship with large-scale fantasy engineering; it is not modern industrial technology. ### Other major peoples and powers - Eldar: A thriving elven civilisation of approximately 18 million, with lifespans around 700–1,200 years. Several royal houses are gathered under a High Sovereign in the western forests of Letharion. - Urakai: A sophisticated and rising orc civilisation of approximately 31 million, organised in clan confederations across eastern plains and highlands. They are not inherently villainous. Their ancient rivalry with the Khazari is political, territorial, industrial and military; trade and alliances remain possible. - Humans: Five major power groupings: Aldermere, Valtoria, the Northern Holds, the Merchant Republics and the Southern Sultanates. - Drakari: Rare dragons, numbering fewer than 10,000, with ancient courts and territories. - Aelwyn: Fae peoples organised around ancient seasonal courts and pacts. - Other peoples: Halflings, Ents, Gnomes, Goblins, Centaurs, Merfolk, Giants and others. Their societies vary: not every people is organised into conventional kingdoms. Khazari and Eldar are both ancient peoples. There is no universally accepted creation story proving which came first. ## Geography and places ### Karak-Varn A vast Khazari mountain city and royal seat, with a current modeled population of roughly 22.8 million (previously 3.8 million in an older model). Known districts and landmarks include: - Crownward: Administrative and royal government quarter. - Ironmarket: Commercial district, including the Copper Kettle tavern. - Upper Artisan Quarter: Home to specialist workshops, including the Silver Anvil. - Lower Artisan District: Residential and craft district, including Edda Coppervein's home. - The Great Stair and Hall of Seven: Major civic landmarks. - Royal Historical Archive: Repository of historical records and restricted research. - The Iron Circle: Military training complex where Sergeant Keldrun teaches civilians. - Old Quarry Access: Quarry site where Borin teaches Gloin practical engineering. ### Ironspine and the eastern mine Several leagues beneath the Ironspine lies an abandoned eastern mine, sealed 63 years ago after reported collapses. Public maps show six levels; an original survey retained by Borin records nine. The lower galleries are unusually smooth, with mathematical pillar arrangements and construction predating the mine itself. Beneath level nine lies a chamber known as the Hall Beneath the Mountain, connected by a narrow passage to a sealed First Throne doorway. ### Crownward private repository Hadrik's research has identified a possible private repository beneath the old Crownward administrative quarter. It was reportedly closed 41 years ago. A possible service entrance was sealed at that time. Access and the survival of the original register remain under investigation. ## History: The First Throne The First Throne was a continent-spanning Khazari civilisation, with a population potentially exceeding 40 million at its height. It had settlements across Ironspine and combined advanced rune-powered machinery, underground agriculture, magical communication networks and sophisticated fortifications. It was not a primitive predecessor. It was one of the greatest civilisations in Khazari history. The First Throne appears to have been deliberately abandoned through an organised process rather than destroyed in a conventional war. The precise reason is unknown. Possible explanations include political dismantling, the deliberate erasure of institutions, and a decision to prevent later rulers from claiming its legitimacy. These remain interpretations, not settled history. ### Sovereigns and the end - Thargrim the Deepfather: Legendary founder or early sovereign. - Thargrim IV: The last universally acknowledged sovereign of the First Throne. His fate is disputed. Three enduring accounts of Thargrim IV's fate: 1. He sacrificed himself to operate a containment system during the evacuation. 2. He was overthrown by nobles after ordering the abandonment. 3. He survived and led a group east into an unknown underground region. None is proven. ### The Silence Below Ancient records describe a sequence of events roughly 3,000 years before the Seven Mountain Thrones were formally established: - c. 3,240 years ago — Deep Resonance: Rhythmic hammering was reported from beneath the civilisation; a settlement was evacuated. - c. 3,190 years ago — Unlit Halls: Magical illumination failed. Survivors reported that something moved in the darkness. - c. 3,160 years ago — Final Sealing: Containment gates were constructed. An ancient warning survives: > Let no descendant mistake the silence of the deep for the absence of what dwells within. Hadrik believes the First Throne may have been trying to escape or contain something it did not understand. He does not know what that was. Theories include a living presence, a magical catastrophe, or something between. None is established. ## Peoples' distinct magical traditions survive the expanded cosmology (creator clarification, 21 November 2026) Binding distinction: The creator explicitly retains the different kinds of magic long associated with Khazari (dwarves), Eldar (elves), Aelwyn Fae, fairy peoples such as Pixies, Gnomes, and other peoples. These are legitimate distinct cultural, practical, possibly innate or supernatural traditions in the setting, not merely interchangeable labels for generic lunar spells. A tradition may have customary methods, ethics, rites, materials, aptitudes and histories, but the detailed disciplines and mechanisms outside already defined Khazari examples remain to be developed—not manufactured retrospectively. Do not merge Aelwyn Fae with Pixies/fairy folk, or make Gnome magic a copy of Khazari rune systems. Individual members of any people are not required to practise any tradition; cross-cultural learning and overlapping magic are possible when consistent with training and ability. Exact already-established Khazari traditions: Runecraft (symbols and enchantments); Deepcraft (stone, earth and subterranean perception/workings); Forgebinding (magical craft and durability); Hearthmagic (warmth, preservation, protection and domestic/settlement uses); Stonecalling (rare mountain-sense/communication); Ancestral Binding (controversial bloodline, oath and hereditary work). Keep them individually distinct, not automatically all lunar or inherently benevolent. Established broad fields include Arcana, Nature, Divination, Bloodcraft, Runecraft and Shadowcraft; these are not exhaustive nor species-exclusive. Moral aspect: Some magical forces are inherently good, some morally grey and some inherently evil, regardless of the caster's intentions. Do not assign an inherent moral alignment to an entire people, civilization, cultural school or broad discipline without specific creator definition; a tradition can contain different techniques and moral natures. This distinction adds nuance to the system without erasing Fae, fairy, Gnome, Eldar, Khazari or other magical heritage. Cosmic sources and knowledge: Moons are literal sources of lunar magic and people know that fact, but not how/why or which moon creates which magical force; some moons show almost no effects, others much stronger. Eryndor independently generates Natural Magic / the World's Breath. Gods of magic can govern or interact with magical forces, not replace moon magic as its source. Do not assign individual moons to cultural traditions or claim that all folk magic derives only from lunar forces without future decisions. Historical mystery, uncertainty and the paused Gloin scene remain protected. ## Magic and Khazari traditions Recognised broad disciplines include Arcana, Nature, Divination, Bloodcraft, Runecraft and Shadowcraft. ### Khazari traditions 1. Runecraft: Symbols direct energy into objects and structures; used to enchant weapons, armour, buildings and mechanisms. 2. Deepcraft: Work with stone, earth and underground structures; practitioners may sense weaknesses, water and subtle changes in rock, and manipulate small amounts of stone. 3. Forgebinding: Enchantment integrated with craftsmanship, producing durable weapons, self-maintaining edges and other crafted effects. 4. Hearthmagic: Warmth, preservation, protection and household or settlement workings. 5. Stonecalling: Rare communication or sensing with a mountain, including sensing movement through rock. 6. Ancestral Binding: Controversial workings linked to bloodlines, oaths and hereditary obligations. The First Throne mastered this discipline. Novices can learn with training and aptitude; these traditions are not exclusive to nobility. ### First Throne script and principles First Throne script is instruction-based. A symbol's meaning depends on its arrangement and context; the same symbol can function differently in another sequence. Gloin has been taught three introductory symbols: - Hold: Maintain a state or position. - Within: Define a boundary or enclosed space. - Until Command: A condition remains active until an authorised instruction is received. Together, an arrangement might express: “Maintain the enclosed state until an authorised command is received.” This does not by itself prove that the command releases the enclosure; it might release, reinforce or change the system. ### Gloin's preliminary aptitude Maela's initial tests indicate: - Strong potential in Deepcraft. - Strong potential in Runecraft. - Possible affinity for Stonecalling. - Forgebinding, Hearthmagic and Ancestral Binding remain untested. During controlled tests, Gloin felt a vibration like a distant heartbeat from an ancient rune, identified a cold section in a broken rune, and briefly elicited a glow from a disconnected binding stone. Maela stopped before overstressing an untrained resonance. These are preliminary signs of aptitude, not mastery or proof of a fully developed supernatural ability. Further Stonecalling tests require a proper grounding stone and controlled conditions. Gloin should not attempt uncontrolled magical experiments. Maela has demonstrated a basic modern Khazari warming rune. Gloin has not yet activated a rune himself. ### Runesmith apprenticeship Gloin has begun a provisional apprenticeship with Maela Deepforge at the Silver Anvil. - Two lessons a week when schedules permit. - First month is provisional; formal apprenticeship depends on progress. - Introductory lessons carry no immediate fee. - Curriculum: First Throne script, modern Khazari runic fundamentals, identifying active and dormant enchantments, magical materials, and controlled practical activation. - Deepcraft testing is separate and requires suitable equipment. - Homework: practise the three symbols Hold, Within and Until Command. Maela estimates that basic usefulness may take a few years, dependable skill around a decade, and accomplishment several decades. ## The eastern mine mystery ### Established physical evidence - The mine was sealed 63 years ago. - Public maps show six levels; Borin's original survey records nine. - The lower galleries contain deliberate First Throne construction. - Beneath level nine is the Hall Beneath the Mountain and a sealed stone doorway. - A margin note dated three days before closure reads: “Sound observed beyond the western wall. No machinery identified.” - The mine was built over an older First Throne structure. - The lower access was reportedly breached 11 nights before Autumn Day 19. The precise nature of the breach is unknown. ### The missing engineers Three officials connected to the original sealing disappeared: - Thrain Coppervein: Chief surveyor; disappeared first. - Orik Feldspar: Structural engineer who supervised sealing; disappeared six weeks later. - Dorin Blackmantle: Royal inspector; last known entering the Crownward district. There were no known bodies or funerals. Families reportedly received no official compensation. Borin was an apprentice engineer during the sealing and helped close the lower access. He retained portions of the original survey. ### Thrain's note A parchment note attributed by Thrain's family to Thrain Coppervein reads: > The lower chambers are not empty.
Orik believes the resonance is structural. I no longer agree.
The western wall responds to the listening stones. Three knocks have been recorded twice now.
I have removed the authority piece from its housing. It cannot be allowed to remain connected. The note is undated. Edda Coppervein says the handwriting is attributed to Thrain by the family. Edda recalls that Thrain carried something wrapped in dark cloth and protected it carefully. Her grandmother remembered Thrain saying Orik wanted to open the door, while Thrain wanted to ensure it stayed closed. Borin independently remembers Thrain carrying a small iron object bearing the Hammer and Crown symbol shortly before sealing. It was small enough to fit in one hand and wrapped in dark cloth. Borin never saw it again. The object may have been the missing authority piece, but this has not been confirmed. ### The containment architecture A surviving survey and its interpretation identify three concentric systems: 1. Outer ring: Pressure regulator distributing force through the mountain. 2. Middle ring: Containment barrier. 3. Innermost ring: Authority mechanism. 4. Attunement mark: A small iron key enclosed within a circle; without it, the authority mechanism cannot function properly. The first three elements and the attunement mark are described in the survey interpretation. It is unknown whether the original builders removed the attunement mark before sealing or whether someone removed it later. The Hammer and Crown is a First Throne authority seal, older than the current Stonehand dynasty. It was once used to authorise magical mechanisms across the First Throne; it is functional, not merely ceremonial. A possible distinction matters: the foundation, pressure distribution and containment barrier might continue working even without the authority piece. The missing piece may govern who can command the system rather than provide its power. This is a plausible interpretation, not proof of the current state of the chamber. ### Listening network and quarry clues Gloin's reading of The Foundations of First Throne Script revealed a diagram of listening stations connected by rune lines. Maela believes these may represent a network of resonance anchors monitoring large underground systems. At an old quarry, Gloin and Borin found: - A survey marker whose modern outer measurements remained intact while older First Throne geometric symbols lay beneath them. - The marker had been deliberately repositioned, though the reason is unknown. - A timber support bore a symbol of three vertical lines and a circular mark. - Maela considers this symbol consistent with a resonance-transfer system, likely more than a simple structural mark. - Borin suspects the quarry marker may belong to a wider listening network and thinks someone may have shifted it to conceal what it measured. This is a hypothesis. ### The unidentified fourth official Borin recalls a fourth engineer or official present during the original sealing: - Tall for a dwarf, with a dark beard. - Wore a silver insignia showing a crossed hammer and a narrow tower. - Had two guards, carried no tools, and argued with Thrain outside the lower access. - Thrain said: “You were not authorised to touch it.” Borin drew a sketch of the insignia and gave it to Gloin. The figure's identity and office are unknown. A connection to Varric Stonehelm is possible but unproven. ## Records, repository and political authority ### Dorin Blackmantle's trail Hadrik found a register entry showing Dorin Blackmantle entering the Crownward district on the 14th day of Winter, Year 3,784, six weeks after Orik disappeared. His recorded destination was the former Chancellor's administrative offices, used for restricted royal inquiries. No departure record survives. Hadrik also found a reference to a restricted report titled Assessment of the Eastern Substructure — Restricted: - Primary author: Thrain Coppervein. - Reviewing authority: Dorin Blackmantle. - Final approval: unrecorded. - Commissioned by: Royal Mining Office. The report is missing from the archive. ### Varric Stonehelm and the private repository Varric Stonehelm, Examiner-General during the old sealing, authorised Dorin's entry. Hadrik found evidence that Varric ordered historical records transferred to a private repository in the months after the mine was sealed. The repository was beneath the old Crownward administrative quarter and was reportedly closed 41 years ago. Hadrik has a surviving copy of an access register listing three names in its final period: - Varric Stonehelm. - An administrative custodian. - A third name deliberately obscured. Hadrik has identified a possible service entrance, sealed when the repository closed. He needs more time to establish whether the original register survives and whether access can be attempted safely. The repository may contain the original assessment and information about the missing engineers, but there is no proof that the records remain there. ### Current mine inspection Lord Chancellor Veyron's office requested that Maela inspect the ancient containment runes. Maela accepted the contract subject to two conditions: 1. Access to surviving architectural records. 2. Permission to inspect the surrounding structure before touching any ancient runes. The office refused to explain the breach in writing. Maela intends to honour the agreement, but will stop if the structure is unsafe or containment may be compromised. She will not activate or alter a mechanism she does not understand. The inspection is scheduled for first light on Autumn Day 22 at the eastern access. Planned party: - Maela Deepforge, specialist in ancient runic architecture. - Edrik Voss, Deputy Examiner, Royal Mining Office. - Captain Roderic Vale, commander of the assigned royal security detail. Maela has not worked with Captain Vale and does not know whether his role is protection, supervision or enforcement. ### Equipment list supplied to Maela - Structural measuring instruments. - Resonance-detection equipment. - Three portable rune-binding frames. - Heavy iron lifting apparatus. - A sealed wooden case listed only as “authorised technical materials”. Maela explains that rune-binding frames hold components in fixed alignment while energy transfers between them. They are used legitimately for restoration, stabilising damaged mechanisms and constructing bindings, but could also reconnect components that were deliberately separated. The sealed case's contents are unknown. Hadrik wants to learn who authorised its transport and who has custody. No evidence currently proves malicious intent. ### Political context - Edrik Voss says the investigation is being handled under Lord Chancellor Veyron's authority. - Edrik says King Durgan IV has not been informed. - The King has not been independently confirmed as uninformed; the statement comes from Edrik. - The Royal Mining Office has sought Borin's original survey. Borin denied possessing it. - Veyron's office has ordered reviews of restricted First Throne historical material. - The Chancellor's motives are unknown. Secrecy may conceal misconduct, or may reflect an effort to contain a genuine danger. Neither interpretation is proven. ## Political and military developments - Valtorian forces have been mobilising near Aldermere's northern frontier; scouts have reportedly been seen near the frontier. - Karak-Varn's military council is expanding recruitment for its eastern garrison in response. - Iron prices are rising amid military demand. - The elven court of Letharion has requested an audience with King Durgan IV. - Rumours from two miners at the Copper Kettle suggested equipment was moving towards the old eastern access and that Royal Mining Office guards had doubled. These were overheard claims, not verified facts. ## Key characters ### Gloin Hammerfeld - People: Khazari dwarf. - Age: 42. - Origin: Common-born, from Karak-Varn. - Occupation: Currently unemployed. - Military status: Not enlisted. - Character path: Open. He may pursue combat, runesmithing, engineering, trade, exploration, politics or another path. - Ancestry: Unknown and intentionally unresolved. Do not invent a hidden lineage or destiny. Current abilities and training - Beginner in combat, with no prior experience striking a person with an axe. - Accepted into Sergeant Keldrun's six-week civilian shield-and-axe course, three sessions per week, beginning Autumn Day 22. - Strong preliminary Deepcraft and Runecraft potential; possible Stonecalling affinity. - Learning First Throne script; the three introductory symbols currently established in his active practical work are Hold, Within and Until Command. On Day 20 he copied, studied and could recognise twelve script symbols from Hadrik's book, but that did not establish understanding, mastery or successful magical operation of all twelve. - Beginning engineering fundamentals with Borin. - Developing practical Deepcraft perception through supervised exercises with Maela; no mastery or reliable Stonecalling ability has been established. Current condition and resources at pause - Healthy, no injuries. - Wealth: 10 silver crowns and 82 copper pieces. One silver crown equals 100 copper pieces. This is the last confirmed balance after Gloin spent 8 silver crowns on a substantial family supper on Autumn Day 21. - Inventory: ordinary clothes, leather boots with worn soles, personal axe, family keepsake (significance not established), borrowed copy of The Foundations of First Throne Script, notebook containing notes and survey-symbol sketches. - Borin retains the original survey; Gloin does not possess it. - Maela has not yet provided the name or route to the quarry that supplied her workshop granite; she agreed to retrieve the old supplier's records. Current commitments and training - Provisional runesmithing apprenticeship with Maela Deepforge at the Silver Anvil, twice weekly when schedules permit; first month carries no immediate fee. - Six-week civilian shield-and-axe course with Sergeant Keldrun, three sessions weekly. Day 21 assessment found good instincts for redirecting pushes, footwork needing work, fair axe control, no combat experience and good discipline. Day 22 session was excused for the mine inspection; the next planned session is Day 23 morning, exact time not established. - Metallurgy lesson with Bruni at 11:30 AM on Autumn Day 23. Bring notebook, work clothes and gloves; first topic is ores, refining and distinguishing good stock from poor material. - Elska has agreed to discreetly research historical attempts to use ambient/Common Magic as an intermediary between disciplines. She will use public records, old works and archived accounts and report to Gloin first; the research has not yet begun. - Continue practising Hold, Within and Until Command. ### Maela Deepforge - Khazari master runesmith and architectural historian, age 143. - Silver-grey hair tightly braided back, with small metal rings in the braids. - Runs The Silver Anvil in the Upper Artisan Quarter. - Expert in ancient runic construction, containment architecture, magical materials and runesmithing. - Blunt, practical, respected and no-nonsense, with occasional dry humour. - Gloin's provisional runesmithing teacher and the specialist contracted for the eastern mine inspection. - Has accepted Veyron's inspection contract under the two conditions recorded above. ### Hadrik Ironvein - Khazari scholar, approximately 176 years old. - Senior researcher at the Royal Historical Archive; has worked there for 112 years and studied First Throne history for roughly 40. - Careful, intellectually honest, loyal to Khazari people and history, but not blindly loyal to the Crown. - Research into First Throne history was administratively restricted about 40 years ago. - Lent Gloin The Foundations of First Throne Script. - Investigating the private repository and obscured access-register name. - Believes the First Throne may have been escaping something beneath its civilisation, but has no definitive answer. ### Borin Ashmantle - Older Khazari with a grey beard and two missing fingers on his left hand. - Former mining engineer and apprentice during the original eastern mine sealing. - Childhood acquaintance of Gloin; practical, cautious, protective and loyal. - Retains the original partial survey hidden at his home. - Teaching Gloin engineering fundamentals: structural weaknesses, tunnel safety, supports, airflow, seepage, tools and surveying. - Has not committed to entering the mine. - Remembers Thrain's wrapped iron object and the unidentified fourth official. ### Sergeant Keldrun Broadshield - Veteran Khazari infantryman, approximately 187 years old, with more than a century of military experience. - Specialises in shield fighting, one-handed axes and hammers, formation combat, confined tunnels and defence against larger opponents. - Teaches at The Iron Circle. - Has accepted Gloin into a six-week civilian course. Three sessions per week, beginning Autumn Day 22. - Initial assessment: promising instincts for balance and redirection; footwork needs refinement; axe control fair; power untested; discipline good. ### Edda Coppervein - Older female dwarf and granddaughter of Thrain Coppervein. - Lives in the Lower Artisan District. - Keeps Thrain's old possessions and the original parchment note attributed to him. - Allowed Gloin to copy the note; the original remains with the family. - Remembers family stories about Thrain's missing iron object and his disagreement with Orik. ### Edrik Voss - Deputy Examiner of the Royal Mining Office. - Approximately 60 years old, black trimmed beard, scar from right ear to jaw, silver royal mining signet. - Sought Borin's original survey and threatened him during the encounter. - Said the western wall was breached 11 nights earlier, watchmen heard three knocks and voices they did not understand, and “something came through”. - Says the Crown wants the matter contained. - Says King Durgan has not been informed and the investigation is being handled under Veyron. - His intentions remain unknown. ### Lord Chancellor Veyron - Senior political official. - His office ordered restricted historical reviews and commissioned Maela's mine inspection. - The Royal Mining Office is acting under his authority, according to Edrik. - His motives and the King's knowledge are unresolved. ### Captain Roderic Vale - Commander of the royal security detail assigned to Maela's inspection. - Maela has not worked with him and does not know his purpose beyond command of the security detail. - Further character details unknown. ## Character and relationship continuity NPCs have independent personalities, loyalties, memories, ambitions and flaws. Their lives do not revolve around Gloin. Relationships change through actions and conversations. Do not assume friendship, trust, hostility or allegiance beyond what has been established. ## Visual canon and reference collection The visual reference collection is intended to preserve consistency across portraits, locations, creatures, weapons, maps and future video scenes. Character faces and distinctive traits should remain recognisable as the story advances; clothing, equipment, injuries, age and status can change with events. ### Gloin — primary portrait reference The user approved a regenerated portrait as the primary reference. Visual traits: - Rugged young adult dwarf. - Reddish-brown long hair and blue-grey eyes. - Strong facial features. - Braided, ringed beard. - His face, hair and general appearance are reference traits. - The portrait includes practical leather and metal gear, fur-lined cloak, mountain rune clasp, rune-etched axe and round shield with mountain emblem. These are visible in the portrait but do not lock the character's future outfit, weapons or equipment. ### Maela — visual reference - Female Khazari master runesmith. - Silver-grey hair tightly braided back. - Small metal rings in the braids. - Clothing is not fixed. ### Borin — visual reference notes - Older dwarf. - Grey beard. - Missing two fingers on the left hand. - Other fine visual details remain open unless separately established. ### Hadrik — visual reference notes - Khazari scholar. - Greying hair has been suggested, but its exact colour and style are not firmly established. ### Visual production rules - ChatGPT generates still images for Eryndor. - fal is reserved exclusively for video generation. - Use established stills as references for consistency when making videos. - Prefer individual portraits and assets over collages. - Rebuild older visuals as individual assets when needed; do not claim an asset exists unless it has actually been generated and retained. - Track visual canon separately from temporary clothing and equipment. - Do not save an image to a persistent reference collection unless the user explicitly asks or approves. ## Campaign rules and continuity - The world is living and independent: kingdoms, armies, merchants, nobles and ordinary people act without waiting for Gloin. - Unexpected encounters, opportunities, disputes, discoveries, celebrations and dangers can occur organically. - Choices have meaningful consequences. Injuries, exhaustion, money, equipment, reputation and death matter. Gloin has no plot armour. - Relationships are earned and remembered. - Gloin is one dwarf among millions. Greatness must be earned; the world must not revolve around him. - Mysteries are independent. Not every strange event is connected to the First Throne. - The user may perform multiple actions in one turn; resolve them sequentially and track elapsed time. - After important NPC conversations, offer suggested dialogue options while allowing freeform responses. - Combat is tactical: positioning, footwork, reach, stamina, weapon handling, armour, terrain, enemy tactics, injury and lasting consequences. - Use a HUD when useful or when something changes, not after every exchange. - Do not predetermine Gloin's clothing, equipment, career, weapons or fighting style. Keep those choices with the user. - When the adventure is paused, no in-world time passes. Do not resume until the user explicitly says to continue. ## Current campaign state: paused Autumn, Day 22, Year 3,847 — approximately 11:25 AM
Location: Royal Historical Archive, Karak-Varn, at Hadrik Ironvein's desk.
Gloin: Arrived with Maela Deepforge. Healthy and uninjured. Last confirmed funds: 10 silver crowns and 82 copper pieces. Hadrik has just greeted Gloin and Maela and asked what they have uncovered. Gloin has not yet answered. The next player action is Gloin's response to Hadrik. The adventure remains paused. No time passes until the user explicitly resumes. ## Open questions and unresolved mysteries - What lies beyond the sealed First Throne doorway? - What exactly happened during the Silence Below? - What came through the western wall, if anything? - Where are Thrain, Orik and Dorin? - What happened to the missing authority piece? - Who was the fourth official bearing the crossed hammer and narrow tower insignia? - What does the obscured third name in the repository register say? - Does the original private repository register still exist? - What is in the sealed wooden case, and who authorised its transport? - Why were the quarry survey marker and listening-symbol alignments altered? - What does Veyron know, and has King Durgan been kept uninformed? - Will Maela's inspection reveal that the containment system is stable, damaged or something else? These questions remain open. Do not resolve them without events or evidence in the adventure. ## Economy, trade goods and living costs The economy of Eryndor is a living system. Prices are not fixed everywhere or forever; they respond to local supply and demand, season, harvests, weather, war, transport routes, taxes, shortages, quality, reputation and the wealth of the buyer or establishment. The following are Karak-Varn baseline prices for ordinary goods and services, not universal prices across Eryndor. Use them as a starting point and adjust naturally when the economy or circumstances change. ### Currency - 100 copper pieces = 1 silver crown. - Gloin's current ledger uses silver crowns and copper pieces. - No higher denomination or conversion is established yet; do not assume one without introducing it in play. ### Lodging and everyday services — Karak-Varn baseline | Good or service | Typical price | | --- | --- | | Shared common-room bed | 2 copper/night | | Basic private room | 5 copper/night | | Comfortable private room | 8 copper/night | | Quality inn room | 1 silver/night | | Bath and hot water | 2 copper | | Simple breakfast | 2–3 copper | | Hearty breakfast | 5 copper | | Hearty meal | 4–6 copper | | Small ale | 2 copper | | Autumn honey brew | 3 copper | These prices are the agreed starting tariff for ordinary Karak-Varn establishments. Better inns, festivals, busy market days, scarcity or unusual service can raise prices; poor conditions, quiet periods, competition or a negotiated arrangement can lower them. ### Trade goods and price tracking Track prices for goods when they become relevant to play, including: - Food and agricultural goods: grain, flour, bread, meat, fish, vegetables, fruit, dairy, preserved foods, livestock and animal feed. - Drink: ale, beer, mead, honey brews, wine, spirits, tea and other local drinks. - Raw materials: iron, copper, tin, silver, gold, coal, timber, stone, leather, wool, salt, clay and other useful materials. - Craft and manufactured goods: tools, weapons, armour, clothing, boots, pottery, furniture, household wares, machinery, runic components and finished craftwork. - Transport and services: pack animals, carts, freight, ferries, stable space, repairs, skilled labour, healing, training, storage, guides and lodging. - Property and rents: rooms, workshops, stalls, storage space, homes, farmland, leases, deposits, upkeep and local fees or taxes. Do not invent a full price catalogue before goods matter. Establish a sensible local baseline when Gloin encounters or needs an item, record it, and use it consistently until circumstances change. ### How prices fluctuate - Supply and demand: shortages raise prices; surplus and competition tend to lower them. - Season and harvest: food, fuel, animal feed and some materials change with the season and harvest quality. - War and politics: mobilisation can raise demand for metal, weapons, armour, horses, food, transport and skilled labour; blockades, tariffs or border tension can disrupt supply. - Transport and geography: distance, dangerous roads, mountain passes, weather and tolls affect delivered prices. - Quality and scarcity: common, serviceable, fine, masterwork, rare and enchanted goods should not share one price. - Local conditions: district, town size, wealth, taxes, guild rules, establishment quality and bargaining affect the final price. - Time: prices may change between visits. Changes should have a cause in the world, not fluctuate randomly just to punish or reward Gloin. ### Campaign accounting rules - Track Gloin's money, purchases, wages, rents, deposits, debts, taxes and sale proceeds consistently. - State meaningful prices before or when Gloin commits to a purchase or rental; do not silently deduct money. - Record recurring costs such as rent, food, stable fees, storage and upkeep when Gloin actually takes them on. - Buying and selling are not automatically at the same price. Older Khazari writings use the phrase the World's Breath for this planetary magic; “Natural Magic” is the broadly used working name. Natural Magic permeates the world: stone, mountains, underground formations, rivers, oceans, plants, forests, living creatures, the atmosphere and natural phenomena. It is the underlying magical energy of an inherently magical planet. Everyone interacts with Natural Magic to some degree, although awareness, aptitude and control vary greatly. Ordinary people may draw on it instinctively or indirectly through their work and surroundings; trained practitioners can sense, channel or shape it deliberately. It is not exclusive to one people or specialist profession. Natural Magic remains present even when lunar influences are weak. Magic never disappears simply because a moon is elsewhere in its orbit. Natural Magic does not automatically make everyone a capable spellcaster, and it does not remove the need for training, judgement, materials, preparation or skill. ### Lunar influences — each moon governs a discipline Moons are actual sources of lunar magic, with unequal, potentially weak or undetectable influence. Specific moon-to-discipline correspondences exist in the cosmology but are not reliably known to the peoples of Eryndor; do not insist every small moon is observably strong or has a known distinct discipline. The moon's orbital position determines the strength of its influence at a given time. Its phase alone is not the determining factor. Different orbital positions and relationships between moons can alter the strength of their respective influences. Alignments may amplify multiple disciplines at once. The lunar system therefore creates changing magical conditions over days, seasons, years and much longer cycles. The complete roster of moons, their names, individual disciplines, orbital periods and influence patterns remains to be developed. Do not prematurely assign every moon a name or magical domain. ### Magical compatibility — disciplines can interact Magical disciplines have inherent affinities and degrees of compatibility. Some naturally cooperate, some require considerable skill to combine, and some resist or interfere with one another. Compatibility exists independently of lunar proximity; aligned moons are not a prerequisite for disciplines to interact. Examples of possible affinities include Runecraft with Deepcraft for structural and magical reinforcement; Healing with Natural Magic for restoration; Elemental Magic with Nature Magic for environmental workings; Illusion with Divination for perception and revelation; and Runecraft with protective or binding magic. These are illustrative relationships, not a complete or universally fixed compatibility chart. Lunar conditions can strengthen or complicate an interaction, but they do not create its underlying compatibility. ### Lunar imbalance and collision risks When moons approach one another unusually closely, their magical influences can interfere, resonate or become unstable. Possible consequences include excessive amplification, uncontrolled surges, unexpected interaction between disciplines, unstable enchantments, disturbances in magical barriers, changes in magical creatures and regional environmental effects. An actual collision could produce a catastrophic magical imbalance. The destruction could release enormous magical energy and alter Eryndor's magical environment for centuries or millennia; it may also create new fragments, smaller moons and further orbital disturbances. These are possible consequences, not a guarantee that every close approach or collision produces the same outcome. Lunar influence affects the whole world, not only spellcasters: magical creatures, enchanted objects, ancient structures, barriers and the natural environment may also be affected. Exceptional celestial conditions do not grant mastery automatically. A novice remains a novice; individual ability, knowledge, training and circumstances determine what can be achieved. ### The lost ancient art of Natural Magic harmonisation In ancient times, practitioners of several civilisations discovered sophisticated ways to harness and refine Natural Magic as a common medium between magical disciplines. They did more than draw additional energy from the planet: they used Natural Magic as an intermediary to strengthen workings, reduce resistance between disciplines, harmonise otherwise difficult combinations and create unified magical workings with far greater efficiency than modern practitioners generally achieve. The ancient method could help connect disciplines beyond their ordinary affinities and could harmonise multiple lunar influences. It did not remove the need for understanding, skill or control. True fusion was distinct from merely casting two spells together or using one discipline to support another: it created a unified working from multiple disciplines. Knowledge of this method was lost for unknown reasons.
